reasoning: According to data from the Congressional Research Service, the Congressional Budget Office, and the Pew Research Center, Congress has only passed all of its regular annual appropriations bills on time (prior to the October 1 start of the fiscal year) in four fiscal years since the current budget process took effect in 1976: FY 1977, FY 1989, FY 1995, and FY 1997. Since the passage of the budget for Fiscal Year 1997 (which occurred in late 1996), Congress has failed to pass all of its regular appropriations bills before the start of the fiscal year, relying instead on stopgap continuing resolutions (CRs) or omnibus spending packages passed after the deadline.
title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
